correction.text: the Sich 'in the Great Meadow (Velykyi Luh) region, spanning the lower Dnieper', 'beyond the rapids' (za porohamy); Khortytsia, Tomakivka, Bazavluk, Mykytyn and Chortomlyk all lie within about 100 km of Zaporizhzhia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1662, but the Zaporozhian Sich page dates the Sich to the 1550s (infobox c. 1552) and lists its seats from Khortytsia (1550s) through Tomakivka, Bazavluk and Mykytyn to Chortomlyk (1652). The page gives no boundary and no area, so only a core round the lower Dnieper is drawn, soft. The page says the Cossacks were included in the Kiev Voivodeship of the Polish-Lithuanian state 1583-1657 and gives the infobox status 'de jure vassal of Poland-Lithuania (1583-1654)'; the Commonwealth dossier owns that relation. After Pereyaslav (1654) the Host was split into the Hetmanate and the more autonomous Zaporizhzhia. Extent is the researcher's reading (confidence 2).

121,080 km2. The pages give no boundary and no area (infobox area not stated on either Zaporozhian page), so the ratio cannot be taken and the extent is unverified. Page: 1657-1687 the Sich was 'practically independent' with 12,000-20,000 Cossacks; 1654 Pereyaslav put the Host under the tsar's protection (Zaporozhian Cossacks page). The shape covers nearly all Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, most of Kirovohrad and Donetsk and parts of Zaporizhzhya, Mykolayiv, Poltava and Kharkiv, which fits the Free Lands 'beyond the rapids' loosely.
493 cells against 495 in 1662 (3 removed, 1 added, under 1% of the area): a few cells at the edge, jitter in Cliopatria's outline; no page opened dates a change in these years.
490 cells against 493 (4 removed, 1 added): a few cells at the edge, jitter in Cliopatria's outline; no page opened dates a change in these years.

491 cells against 490 (1 removed, 2 added): a few cells at the edge, jitter in Cliopatria's outline; no page opened dates a change in these years. The Ottoman dossier records a 213-cell 'loss' of right-bank Ukraine to the Zaporozhians in 1677 (confidence 1), but this shape gains two cells in 1677, so that counterpart is not borne out here.

120,042 km2, unchanged to 1751 (68 years, 490 cells): a single outline for the whole of the Sich's later life. The pages date, within these years, the 1667 condominium of Russia and Poland-Lithuania (Treaty of Andrusovo page: 'The Zaporozhian Sich was recognized as a condominium of both states'), the destruction of the Chortomlyk Sich in 1709, the Oleshky Sich in the Crimean Khanate 1711-1728 (infobox: de jure vassal of the Ottoman Empire 1711-1734) and the return under Russian protection in 1734 ('regained all of their former lands'), but none gives a boundary, so the outline stays unverified. During 1711-1734 the seat lay outside the shape. The Nikopol and Kamianka-Dniprovska seats of 1639-1775 lie partly outside the outline (reading of the gazetteer cells, not of a page).

98,379 km2 against 120,042 in 1751: 91 cells (about 23,000 km2, 30.7-36.1 E, 48.5-49.8 N) drop out, chiefly in Kirovohrad (86 to 49 cells), Poltava (46 to 4) and Cherkasy (7 to 0). That is the land of New Serbia: the page says it was 'settled in 1752 by Serbian immigrants from the Military Frontier' and 'located on the Russian-Polish border and on the land of the Zaporizhian Sich', 'mostly in present-day Kirovohrad Oblast, with parts in Cherkasy, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts'. The shape is right; the ledger carries the loss to the Russian Empire.

98,424 km2, one cell more than 1752; no event on the pages opened. The Sich page records no territorial change 1752-1775; population 'about 52,000' in the steppes in 1768 and 'c. 183,700' in 1762 for the Sich (infobox).

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years are extended from 1774 to 1775 because the Sich ended with the manifesto of 3 August 1775, not in 1774

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria ends the row in 1774. The Sich page: 'Russian forces under Peter Tekeli surrounded the Sich on 5 June. The 3 August 1775 manifesto disbanded it and annexed it to Novorossiya Governorate, and the Sich was razed.' (the Cossacks page gives the attack as 15 May to 8 June and the court council decision of 7 May 1775). The 1774 Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca is mentioned on the Cossacks page but has no Zaporozhian territorial clause there.

region.text: the Sich 'in the Great Meadow (Velykyi Luh) region, spanning the lower Dnieper', 'beyond the rapids' (za porohamy); Khortytsia, Tomakivka, Bazavluk, Mykytyn and Chortomlyk all lie within about 100 km of Zaporizhzhia

ledger.note: 1552: the Zaporozhian Sich arises on the lower Dnieper beyond the rapids. The infobox gives 'Established' c. 1552 and the text dates the Sich to the 1550s ('Dmytro Vyshnevetsky built Khortytsia Castle'; 'Crimean Tatar forces destroyed the fortress in 1558'); 'Preceded by: Wild Fields'. The page gives a seat, not a boundary; the core is a 100 km radius.

c. 1564: the Host's seat moves to the Tomakivka Sich, an island in the Dnieper near Marhanets (table: c. 1564-1593), after Khortytsia was destroyed in 1558; the page dates no Sich for the years between.
1593: 'The Tatars razed the Tomakivka Sich'; the Bazavluk Sich (1593-1638) becomes the seat.
1639: the Mykytyn Sich (1639-1652) replaces the Bazavluk Sich, 'destroyed by a Polish expeditionary force' in 1638.
1652: 'The Chortomlyk Sich was built at the mouth of the Chortomlyk River' (table: 1652-1709); Khmelnytsky had captured the Mykytyn Sich in 1648.

1709: the Chortomlyk Sich is destroyed (the Sich page: before Poltava; the Cossacks page: Peter ordered the destruction after Poltava) and the Kamianka Sich is founded at the mouth of the Kamianka River (table: 1709-1711).
1711: the Kamianka Sich is destroyed 'by the Russian government'; the Cossacks flee to the Crimean Khanate and found the Oleshky Sich (1711-1728), under Crimean-Ottoman protection (Cossacks page).
c. 1728: a Kamianka Sich is again the seat (table: c. 1728-1734; the table also lists a Chortomlyk Sich for 1728-1730), leaving Oleshky.

1734: 'In 1734, they were allowed to return to the Russian Empire' and built the Nova Sich near the former Chortomlyk Sich (1734-1775); the Cossacks page adds that they 'regained all of their former lands, privileges, laws and customs'.

region.text: the land of New Serbia, 'on the land of the Zaporizhian Sich', mostly in present-day Kirovohrad Oblast with parts of Cherkasy, Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts

ledger.note: 1752: New Serbia is settled on the north-western Zaporozhian lands. 'settled in 1752 by Serbian immigrants from the Military Frontier', 'on the land of the Zaporizhian Sich', 'mostly in present-day Kirovohrad Oblast, with parts in Cherkasy, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts'; 1752-1764 it was subordinated to the Governing Senate and Military Collegium. The year and the land are the page's; the outline lost is Cliopatria's 1751 shape minus its 1752 shape.

region.text: the Zaporozhian lands annexed to the Novorossiya Governorate

ledger.note: 1775: the Zaporozhian Sich is abolished. 'The 3 August 1775 manifesto disbanded it and annexed it to Novorossiya Governorate, and the Sich was razed.' (Russian forces under Peter Tekeli surrounded the Sich on 5 June; the fleeing Cossacks formed the Danubian Sich, Cossacks page.)

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654-1667)
wars.outcome: The Truce of Andrusovo, signed 9 February 1667 (O.S. 30 January) at Andrusovo near Smolensk, partitioned the Hetmanate along the Dnieper (Left-bank Ukraine to Russia, Right-bank Ukraine to Poland-Lithuania, Kiev to Russia for two years) and recognised the Zaporozhian Sich as a condominium of both states.
wars.note: The page does not name the Sich as a belligerent; it is listed because the truce fixed its status. Kiev passed to Russia permanently in 1686 for 146,000 rubles (same page). No contest event: a condominium is not a fought-over zone, and the status belongs in the two suzerains' dossiers.

wars.name: Battle of Poltava
wars.outcome: The Zaporozhian Host under Kost Hordiienko joined Hetman Ivan Mazepa against Russia; after the Russian victory Peter ordered a retaliatory destruction of the Sich (Chortomlyk), and the Host moved to the Kamianka Sich.
wars.note: The page dates only 1709; the war the battle belongs to was not opened. The Sich page says the Chortomlyk Sich was destroyed before the battle and the Kamianka Sich was founded in 1709.

wars.name: Pruth campaign and Treaty of the Pruth
wars.outcome: Treaty signed 23 July 1711 on the river Prut: Azov returned to the Ottoman Empire, Taganrog and several fortresses (Kodak, Novobogoroditskaya, Kamenny Zaton on the Dnieper) to be demolished. The Zaporozhians, after 'the early successes of their 1711 attack on Russia', were defeated and fled to the Crimean Khanate, founding the Oleshky Sich.
wars.note: The Pruth page does not say who held suzerainty over the Cossacks (it names Devlet II Giray, Orlyk and Charles XII as wanting protection for the Cossacks); the 1711 attack and the Oleshky Sich are from the Cossacks and Sich pages. Of the Treaty of Adrianople (1713) the page says Peter 'took his hand away' from Ukraine and the Zaporizhian Sich.

wars.name: Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich

zones.text: the Zaporozhian lands and the Sich

wars.outcome: Russian forces under Peter Tekeli surrounded the Sich on 5 June 1775; the manifesto of 3 August 1775 disbanded the Host and annexed its lands to the Novorossiya Governorate; the Sich was razed and the Cossacks fled to the Danube Delta.
wars.note: The Cossacks page gives the decision of 7 May 1775 and the attack as 15 May to 8 June; the Sich page gives 5 June for the encirclement.

certainty.note: Only a core round the lower Dnieper is drawn; the pages give no boundary, and the Sich page says 'no formal boundaries are stated' for the Free Lands.

The Liberties had no surveyed boundary on the pages opened (only river mouths and the rapids). The north-western line from 1752 follows the settlement of New Serbia, an imperial province, but the page gives no survey.

notes:
Written for batch eu-16-i from five content pages (budget 5; the Nova Serbia disambiguation page and one failed URL, New_Serbia_(Ukraine), were extra fetches). No page gives a Zaporozhian boundary or an infobox area, so every Cliopatria outline is 'ok' with the extent unverified; the one border move, 1752, is explained by New Serbia.
START 1552: Cliopatria's row begins 1662; the Zaporozhian Sich page dates the Sich to the 1550s (infobox c. 1552). The dossier starts at 1552 with a soft 100 km core (new keyframe zaporozhian-cossacks_1552, 1552-1661, confidence 2); the Don Cossacks row (1552-1641) starts in the same year. Drop the keyframe if the renderer should not draw a Cossack core inside the Commonwealth (1583-1657 'included in the Kiev Voivodeship').
STATUS RELATIONS the Zaporozhian pages give but that belong in the suzerains' dossiers (this schema has no event for the vassal's side): infobox 'de facto independent; de jure vassal of Poland-Lithuania (1583-1654), Muscovy (1654-1709), the Ottoman Empire (1711-1734), and the Russian Empire (1734-1775)'; 1667 condominium of Russia and Poland-Lithuania (Treaty of Andrusovo). Suggested: vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart zaporozhian-cossacks in polish-lithuanian-commonwealth (1583-1654), tsardom-of-russia (1654-1709), ottoman-empire (1711-1734) and russian-empire (1734-1775).
CROSS-CHECKS for the gap-fillers: (1) ottoman-empire's 1677 'loss' of right-bank Ukraine to zaporozhian-cossacks (confidence 1) is not borne out by this shape (two cells added in 1677). (2) ottoman-empire records 1739 'Zaporozhye region' ceded to Russia (Treaty of Nis); the Sich pages opened here have the Host under Russian protection from 1734 and do not mention 1739. (3) The Cossacks page says the Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca (1774) 'annexed the Crimean Khanate into Russia', which the crimean-khanate dossier dates 1783; not used here.
PAGES DISAGREE on the Chortomlyk Sich: destroyed before Poltava (Sich page), 'after the defeat at the Battle of Poltava Peter ordered a retaliatory destruction' (Cossacks page), and the Sich 'destroyed in 1711 by the Russian government' (Sich page, which may mean the Kamianka Sich). The ledger keeps 1709 for the move to Kamianka and 1711 for Oleshky.
CAPITAL COORDINATES are approximate positions of the sites (now largely under the Kakhovka reservoir), not from the pages; the years are the Sich page's table. The table has overlaps (Chortomlyk 1728-1730 and Kamianka c. 1728-1734) that the capitals list resolves to Kamianka.
NEEDED ELSEWHERE: a Cossack Hetmanate dossier (1648-1764, 'In 1764 Russian authorities abolished the Hetmanate'; the 1654 split and the 1667 partition along the Dnieper), the Danubian Sich (1775-1828), New Serbia (1752-1764), and the Danube Delta region in the gazetteer. Cliopatria has no row for any of them.
